title: What's living on your bath towel

beats.vo: Is your bath towel a germ hotel?
beats.visual: Clean white frame, receipt-paper texture. A folded towel on a bathroom shelf in soft window light; a receipt strip prints out at frame edge with a question mark. Slow lateral slide across the towel's loops. Reads in under 2 s.

beats.vo: The claim: use disposable towels for ideal skin. Let's check the receipt.
screen: CLAIM: disposable towels for ideal skin
beats.visual: The receipt strip prints the claim in Courier Prime, printer ticks on each word. Camera holds on the printing line; a hand of mid-brown skin tone lifts the towel (touch motivates the move).

beats.vo: Line one. Towels can pass on germs.
beats.visual: Receipt line 1 prints. Macro push-in on the towel weave down to fibre scale: soft translucent shapes sit in the loops. Motivated macro push on the word germs.

beats.vo: Staph, a common skin germ, can spread when you touch something that carries it. Like a towel.
beats.visual: Macro slide across a forearm of deep brown skin, then a fingertip touches a towel corner; a few teal microbe shapes transfer from towel loop to fingertip. Lateral slide follows the touch.

beats.vo: Usually, it's minor, and it stays in the skin.
beats.visual: Macro of skin surface, light teal outline of microbes sitting on the surface layer only. Slow hold, no move.

beats.vo: Ringworm, a skin fungus, can ride on a towel too. It thrives where it's warm and humid.
beats.visual: Fair-skinned shoulder macro, thread-like fungus shapes drawn on the surface; a warm steam haze drifts into frame as the bathroom warms. Slow lateral slide.

beats.vo: That's why dermatologists say never share towels.
beats.visual: Two towels hang side by side on separate hooks; a receipt strip prints 'Never share towels' and a Verified Teal HOLDS UP stamp lands on line 1. Static medium shot, stamp slams on the word share.

beats.vo: That line holds up. But it's about sharing, and about infections.
beats.visual: Stamp stays; receipt strip prints 'sharing' and 'infections' tags in Slate. Slow push-in on the stamp.

beats.vo: Line two. Your own towel, on your own skin, for ideal skin. Different question.
screen: LINE 2 · your own towel, your own skin
beats.visual: Receipt line 2 prints. A person of light-olive skin dries their cheek with a towel in close-up; camera drifts laterally with the towel pat.

beats.vo: Dermatologists say pat your skin dry with a clean towel. Rubbing can irritate skin.
beats.visual: Macro side-by-side: left a gentle pat on dark brown skin, skin surface calm; right rough rubbing, a pink flush appears. Split frame, locked off.

beats.vo: Clean towel. The word disposable never shows up.
beats.visual: The receipt prints 'clean' in teal; the word 'disposable' prints beneath in Slate with a thin strike-through line, then fades. Static over a towel stack.

beats.vo: So disposable towels for better skin? None of the guidance I read says so.
beats.visual: Slow push-in on a plain unlabelled stack of paper towels beside a cotton towel; both stay unbranded. Receipt strip prints 'no source found'.
Receipt total line prints; a Slate UNKNOWN stamp lands in Courier Prime. Printer tick, hold 1 s stillness.

beats.vo: Clean, dry, and not shared is what the guidance actually says. Disposable? No receipt.
beats.visual: The receipt strip finishes printing the one-line summary; camera pulls back to show the whole strip under a towel on a shelf. Calm pull-back.

beats.vo: If your skin needs a closer look, a dermatologist can check yours.
beats.visual: Gentle lateral slide across a range of skin tones, final frame on the end-card text. Hold 1.8 s.

end_card.text: Receipt total: UNKNOWN · Towels can pass on some infections, so don't share. Disposable towels for better skin? No receipt. Education, not medical advice.

cover.headline: What's living on your bath towel
